results.title: Wall Type Issue, Especially in Maine | ResStock

item.text:
Yes. ResStock has a documented **Geometry Wall Type error for Maine**, traced to mislabeled county tax assessor data. For example, the 2024 Release 2 data classify Maine’s single-family detached homes as approximately **10% wood frame, 12% brick, and 78% concrete/CMU**—a distribution the team confirmed is unrealistic. The issue report says no fix has been implemented and that all published datasets are believed affected. [Official issue report](https://natlabrockies.github.io/ResStock.github.io/docs/resources/explanations/Issue_Wall_Type_Especially_Maine.html)

The team recommends:

- **For wall type or exterior finish distributions:** use nearby-state ResStock results, especially **Vermont and New Hampshire**, as proxies.
- **For measures whose eligibility depends on wall type:** reweight Maine results using nearby-state wall type distributions, or use nearby-state measure results directly. This matters for upgrades such as insulation applied only to wood-frame walls, whose applicability in Maine may be understated. [Recommendations and impacts](https://natlabrockies.github.io/ResStock.github.io/docs/resources/explanations/Issue_Wall_Type_Especially_Maine.html)

The team currently does **not** expect significant effects on baseline energy consumption, emissions, or bills, but its impact investigation remains incomplete. Document the proxy or reweighting method when reporting Maine wall type results.
